morning_concept_explanation: Day 1 of the current challenge configuration is House Robber. Use it to teach the transferable idea behind a take-vs-skip recurrence: at each position, either skip the current value or take it together with the best valid result from two positions earlier. Focus on deriving the state and transition instead of memorizing the formula, and compare the O(n) time, O(n) space version with the O(1) space optimization.
evening_feedback: Day 1 challenge status: both Alidin and Emiliya have submitted. The available backup contains their submission links, but not their submitted code, so do not claim a specific approach or complexity for either participant. The challenge configuration identifies House Robber as Day 1; use that as the authoritative challenge source. The main takeaway should be recognizing the take-vs-skip decision and being able to derive why the current house conflicts with the previous one.
next_morning_concept: Binary trees: BFS and the level-by-level invariant
next_morning_concept_explanation: Day 2 of the current challenge configuration is Binary Tree Level Order Traversal. Introduce breadth-first search (BFS) as processing a tree level by level, using a queue and maintaining the invariant that the queue contains the next frontier to process.
next_evening_feedback: Review Day 2 by asking the participant to explain why the queue produces level order, how to separate one level from the next, and the resulting time and space complexity.
